message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that involves a lot more than just a coat of paint. Here’s a quick rundown of what it takes and how long it typically takes: | Step | What Happens | Time Required | |------|--------------|---------------| | **Preparation** | • Clean the metal surface (often with high‑pressure water or steam).
• Remove old paint, rust, and debris.
• Apply primer and protective coatings. | 1–2 weeks (depending on weather and crew size) | | **Painting** | • Apply multiple layers of paint (usually 3–4 coats).
• Workers use scaffolding, rope access, and sometimes drones for hard‑to‑reach spots. | 2–3 weeks | | **Inspection & Touch‑ups** | • Inspect for missed spots, uneven coverage, or damage.
• Perform touch‑ups and final quality checks. | 1 week | | **Cleanup & Restoration** | • Remove scaffolding, clean up debris, restore any disturbed areas. | 1 week | **Total:** Roughly **5–7 weeks** for a full repaint, assuming a dedicated crew of 30–50 workers, good weather, and no major complications. ### Why the Eiffel Tower is Painted Every 7–10 Years - **Corrosion Protection:** The tower is made of wrought iron, which rusts if exposed to moisture. Paint acts as a barrier. - **Maintenance Schedule:** The French Ministry of Culture and the Société d’Exploitation de la Tour Eiffel (SETE) schedule repainting every 7–10 years to keep the structure safe and visually appealing. - **Historical Preservation:** The paint also preserves the tower’s iconic appearance for future generations. ### Real‑World Example During the 2019–2020 repainting, the tower was covered in a new “Eiffel Tower White” paint. The project took about **6 weeks** from start to finish, involving around **40 workers** and a crew of **30 painters**. The work was carefully staged to minimize disruption to visitors and to ensure safety. --- **Bottom line:** Painting the Eiffel Tower is a multi‑week project that requires careful planning, skilled labor, and a lot of protective measures. It typically takes **5–7 weeks** from start to finish.
